points.detail: #1: indexed (a self-consistent release decision closeout governance index).
#2: index-blocked (a self-consistent release decision closeout governance index).

governanceIndexTrend.detail: TREND-BLOCKED: a BLOCKING or untrustworthy history — a considered window is tampered, the latest usable window is INDEX-BLOCKED, the blocked count exceeds the threshold, or `--strict-watch` escalated a watch trend. Do NOT treat the recent governance as consistently closed until the cause is resolved.

reasons.detail: The latest (newest) usable window's OWN index verdict is `index-blocked` — its most recent governance history was tampered / blocked. The recent history is not consistently closed: reconcile the latest window's block and re-index it before relying on the history.

The number of `index-blocked` windows in the history exceeds `--max-blocked`. A recurring blocked window is a governance regression, not noise: reconcile the blocked windows (or raise `--max-blocked` only if the blocked history is understood and accepted) before treating the history as closed.

The newest usable window's index verdict is WORSE than the oldest usable window's (a worse index posture after an earlier cleaner one) — the recent arc degraded. Investigate what changed between the recent windows before relying on the history.

checklist.detail: A window in the history is `index-blocked` (its governance history was tampered / blocked, or `--strict-watch` escalated a watch one): do NOT treat that review period as consistently closed. Reconcile the block and re-index that window before relying on the history.

The recent arc is worsening (the newest window is worse than the earliest usable window): investigate what changed between the recent review periods and resolve the regression before relying on the history. Archive this trend as the record of that review.

Keep this content-free trend as the local release-decision-closeout-governance-index governance review SUMMARY. It is NOT a legal audit log, a compliance attestation, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, or a deployment / promotion ledger; keep those separately.

guidance: Wire this as a SCHEDULED or on-demand GOVERNANCE summary (per quarter / half-year), NOT a per-release gate: run `worker:release-decision-closeout-governance-index` per review window and archive each window, then hand a bounded history (oldest first, newest last) here and render `--text` into a review artifact / `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Fail the review on exit 4 (a blocked / untrustworthy history), surface exit 3 (a watch / degrading history) and exit 2 (an incomplete history) for review, and treat exit 0 (a coherent history) as consistently closed — never as an authorization.

Keep the history bounded and explicit: `--max-indexes=N` caps the newest N windows (older windows are dropped from the history, and the count dropped is surfaced, never silent); `--max-open=N` / `--max-incomplete=N` / `--max-blocked=N` (each default 0) tolerate a bounded number of non-`indexed` windows before the accumulation escalates; `--strict-watch` escalates any watch trend to a hard block for a high-assurance review. Direction is derived from ORDERED INPUT POSITIONS (oldest first, newest last), never from any ingested timestamp.

Archive this trend (and the underlying governance-index windows) as CI artifacts: it is a content-free governance SUMMARY, not a substitute for the windows it summarizes, nor for your legal audit trail, compliance log, external approval / signing, storage retention, or release-promotion processes — keep each of those in its own dedicated system.

Enforce promotion out of band: this trend SUMMARIZES a history of the content-free governance-index windows supplied, but recording a legal audit trail, obtaining an external approval / signature, proving reviewer identity, and promoting a deployment are operator / CI / legal actions this offline summarizer never performs.
caveats: This is a RELEASE DECISION CLOSEOUT GOVERNANCE INDEX TREND SUMMARY: it INGESTS a bounded history of content-free `pdfxyz.release-decision-closeout-governance-index/1` windows a release pipeline produced, RE-VALIDATES each against ITSELF, and folds them into ONE bounded trend verdict + follow-up checklist. It is a local content-free governance-index TREND SUMMARY over governance-index windows — NOT a legal audit log, a compliance attestation, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, or a deployment / promotion ledger.

It is offline and READ-ONLY: it makes NO network call, reads NO secret, bucket, or object, RUNS no gate / index / decision / trend / plan / receipt / closeout / governance itself, and NEVER signs, approves, publishes, promotes, deploys, notifies, deletes, prunes, uploads, or mutates any window, record, artifact, object, or deployment. A `trend-stable` trend authorizes nothing; it only reports that the content-free governance-index windows supplied on THIS host trended consistently closed over the review history.

A `trend-stable` trend REQUIRES a coherent bounded history: the latest usable window an `indexed` index, no tampered / unreadable window, the open / incomplete / blocked counts within their thresholds, and a non-degrading arc. It FAILS CLOSED: a tampered window, an `index-blocked` latest / threshold breach, or a `--strict-watch` escalation makes the trend `trend-blocked`; an `index-open` latest / threshold breach or a degrading arc makes it `trend-watch`; an unreadable window, an `index-incomplete` latest / threshold breach, or zero usable windows makes it `trend-incomplete`. It never fabricates a clean trend from thin or untrusted history.

It re-derives each ingested window's index verdict from the window's OWN recorded ledger (reusing the Phase 70 rollup reducer) AND re-checks those counts against the window's own per-record sequence + window arithmetic, and treats any disagreement as a TAMPER (`trend-blocked`). This re-derivation is TAMPER-EVIDENCE over content-free data, NOT a cryptographic signature — there is no signing key and no attested identity, so the trend proves neither authorship nor approval, and a set of fully self-consistent fabricated windows is out of its scope.

It emits only bounded enums, small counts, an ISO stamp, and app-authored prose — so it carries no reviewer name or email, no filename, path, object key, bucket, URL, endpoint, region, job / user id, IP, token, raw ref, raw label, raw note, commit URL, size, byte, or digest, even from a hostile input; it never echoes an ingested window's own stamp, and it never echoes an input file path, even on an error.
It is not malware scanning, sanitization, authorization, cloud validation, or deletion proof of any request or object, and it deletes, uploads, promotes, approves, or mutates nothing.

receipt.disclosure: This is a content-free governance-index TREND SUMMARY ONLY — NOT a legal / compliance sign-off, an external approval / signature, an identity proof, a deployment authorization, a promotion ledger, an incident record, or an audit log. It ingests a bounded history of previously produced governance-index summaries and records whether the recent release decision closeout governance trended consistently closed; it authorizes and proves nothing, and it attests no person's identity.
